name: Wood decayer confined to one piece of wood
description: A dense mycelium that arrives by spore and stays inside its log, trunk or bale, with thick fronts and no cords. Territories are bounded by zone lines and it fights its neighbours at the boundary.

tip_speed.note: middle of the 1 to 10 mm/day front speed given for unit-restricted wood decayers (research/02 section 4), about 5.5 mm/day. The type species Pleurotus ostreatus is faster (500 um/h at 30 C, research/08 [18]) and keeps its own value

branch_angle_sd.note: as for the type species Pleurotus ostreatus: default from Hopkins & Boswell 2012 (79 +/- 10 deg, research/09); not measured for the type species

sensitivity.note: how strongly tips turn away from crowding; model coefficient

fusion_probability.note: chance a tip that meets a hypha fuses and does not cross; no measurement found

density_cap.note: hyphal density at which branching stops; tuning value

explore.note: stays inside its wood; tuning value

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / 100 so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

inactivation_rate.note: as for the type species Pleurotus ostreatus: from Rhizoctonia solani (Boswell et al. 2003, research/09); not this species (0.5 per day)

degradation_rate.note: none seen in 15 h in R. solani; small value so dead hyphae clear

passive_transport.note: diffusion between neighbouring segments; measured diffusion inside hyphae (1 to 2 x 10^-9 m2/s, research/10) is several times faster than the passes allow

soil.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

wood.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

litter.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

root.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

agar.note: how well it feeds on this substrate; from its ecology, not measured

transport_speed.note: as for the type species Pleurotus ostreatus: no measurement for the type species; near the 14.4 mm/h ceiling for motor transport and the 18 mm/h mass flow measured in Neurospora (research/10)

t_opt.note: typical optimum near 28 C across 37 wood-decay isolates, range 22 to 32 C (research/06 [3]); the type species Pleurotus ostreatus is at 30 C

t_min.note: no measurement found; the 37 isolates of research/06 [3] all grew at 10 C

cold_drop.note: cultivated basidiomycetes commonly need a downshift of 5 to 10 C (research/05 [2][5]); low end used. Perennial brackets may need none; the type species uses 8 C

wobble.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

avoidance.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

fusion_probability.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

uptake.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

turn.note: tuning value for the 4K engine; not a measured quantity

spike_interval.note: from the type species Pleurotus ostreatus: about one spike per 70 min in mycelium on hemp, extracellular (research/04 [17]); other members range from 41 min (Schizophyllum) to 102 min (Flammulina) (research/04 [16])

spike_duration.note: from the type species Pleurotus ostreatus: median 62 s (research/04 [17])

spike_amplitude.note: from the type species Pleurotus ostreatus: median 0.48 to 0.51 mV, extracellular (research/04 [17])

score.note: early secondary colonisers such as Trametes versicolor sit in the middle of the hierarchy: they replace primary colonisers and are replaced by, or deadlock with, cord formers (research/06 section 2.5 [4]; research/02 section 4)
